subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: For source-channel turns that emit assistant text before or between tool calls, should OpenClaw deliver classified user-facing text, keep it private with an agent-visible undelivered marker, or require message(action=send) for all channel-visible output?
rationale: The source and related reports show both security/UX leakage and transcript-vs-delivery mismatch risks, and the safe default affects existing channel behavior, direct chats, cron delivery, and message-tool-only upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Private plus delivery marker
options.body: Keep internal/pre-tool text private by default, but inject or persist delivery-status context so later agent turns cannot assume suppressed text was seen by the user.

options.title: Deliver classified pre-tool text
options.body: Flush text classified as user-facing before tool execution while preserving commentary/reasoning suppression and adding regression tests for leak variants.

options.title: Require message tool
options.body: Move channel-visible output to explicit message(action=send) semantics with an upgrade path for existing automatic direct/source-chat deployments.

recommendation.title: Private plus delivery marker
recommendation.body: Keep internal/pre-tool text private by default, but inject or persist delivery-status context so later agent turns cannot assume suppressed text was seen by the user.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest current-main routing signal from the sampled source-reply and embedded delivery history, and the decision spans product/security defaults rather than a narrow code defect.
